title: A-Frame Debris Hut Thermal Shelter (Emergency Primitive Bivouac)
summary: Surviving sub-zero wilderness without fire requires trapping your metabolic body heat like a heavy down sleeping bag. By interlocking an A-frame ridgepole spine and banking a 1-meter mound of dry forest leaves, this debris hut maintains internal warmth even in freezing rains and howling gales.

materials.name: Main Ridgepole (Spine Timber)
materials.desc: One straight, sturdy hardwood limb (3.0–3.5m length, 10–15cm diameter) capable of bearing deadweight

materials.name: Y-Bipod Fork Sticks & Rib Poles
materials.desc: Two 1.5m chest-high Y-forked branch posts and 40–50 arm-length (1–1.5m) rib branches for the wall lattice

materials.name: Dry Forest Debris (Thermal Mass)
materials.desc: 2–3m³ of bone-dry leaves, pine needles, dry ferns, and shredded bark

steps.title: Step 1: Erect A-Frame Bipod and Seat Ridgepole
steps.description:
1. **Interlock Y-Bipod Posts**: Stand two sturdy Y-forked branches facing each other to create a stable tripod apex **0.8–1.0m above ground**.
2. **Anchor Ridgepole Spine**: Seat one end of the **3.0–3.5m hardwood ridgepole** securely into the bipod fork and ground the tail end firmly into the windward soil.
3. **Verify Coffin Sizing**: Ensure the interior width leaves only **one fist of clearance (about 10cm)** around your shoulders when lying down.
steps.actionNote: > Volume Minimization Rule: An oversized interior cannot be heated by human body warmth. Keep the interior strictly form-fitting to trap thermal air pockets.
svgLabels: Strict Coffin Spec: max +10cm (1 fist) body clearance

deepDive.title: Interior Volume Minimization & Metabolic Radiative Heat Trapping
deepDive.text: The sole thermal heat source in a non-heated emergency shelter is human basal metabolic radiation (**approx. 100W**). An oversized interior creates a convective sink that exhausts body heat. Sizing the cabin strictly like a coffin eliminates air draft and holds trapped air at a comfortable temperature.

steps.title: Step 2: Lay Rib Poles at 45° and Pack 40cm Dry Leaf Bed
steps.description:
1. **Lay 45-Degree Rib Lattice**: Lean 40–50 rib sticks against both sides of the spine at a steep **45°–60° angle** like closely spaced ribs.
2. **Pack 40cm Dry Leaf Mattress**: Pile bone-dry leaves, pine needles, and dry grass over the bare ground to **at least 40cm depth**.
3. **Verify Compressed Thickness**: Lie down to compress the bed; verify that **at least 20cm of dead-air insulation** remains between your back and the soil.
steps.actionNote: > Conductive Heat Shield: Bare frozen soil conducts body heat away 20 times faster than air. A thick dry mattress is even more vital than the roof.
svgLabels: Block ground conduction: keep ≥15~20cm compressed bed

deepDive.title: Ground Thermal Conduction & Dead Air Space Insulation Mechanics
deepDive.text: Direct contact with cold soil drains core body heat **20 times faster** than still air. Dry leaves contain countless microscopic dead-air pockets with an exceptionally low thermal conductivity of **0.025 W/m·K**, creating an impenetrable barrier against ground frost.

steps.title: Step 3: Mound 60–90cm Debris Walls and Seal Entrance
steps.description:
1. **Weave Twig Underlay**: Cover rib poles with fine dry twigs to prevent leaves from falling through into the sleeping space.
2. **Bank 60–90cm Debris Wall**: Mound dry leaves from the ground up to the ridgepole to a **depth of 60–90cm (full arm's length)**.
3. **Weight Down with Armor Branches**: Lay heavy dead branches across the mound in a crosshatch pattern to pin down leaves against storm gusts.
4. **Seal Entrance with Leaf Plug**: Crawl inside feet first and pull a dense bundle of dry leaves into the doorway to block all outside drafts.
steps.actionNote: > Bone-Dry Rule: Mixing wet leaves ruins insulation and causes severe evaporative chilling. Use exclusively crisp, dry forest floor debris.
svgLabels: 60~90cm dry leaf mound + full entrance plug seal
DEAD AIR CORE & PLUG SEAL (Thermal Chamber)

deepDive.title: Steep Slope Water Shedding & Multi-Layered Natural Shingling
deepDive.text: When dry debris is piled **60cm thick** on a **steep 45° slope**, leaf surface waxes and interlocking multi-layer structures act like roof shingles, forcing rainwater to run down the outside without penetrating the sleeping core.

fatalMistake.title: Fatal Error: Building an Oversized Cabin & Mixing Wet Debris
fatalMistake.description: Raising the ceiling for sitting comfort creates a large air pocket that human basal metabolism (80–100W) cannot heat. Furthermore, packing damp leaves into the floor or walls turns the shelter into a conductive evaporative cooler.
fatalMistake.consequence: Consequence: Combined conductive and convective heat loss drops core body temperature below 30°C during sleep, causing fatal hypothermia.

outcome.title: Completed A-Frame Debris Hut Thermal Shelter
outcome.description: A 2.5m heavy ridgepole and 45° rib frame blanketed by 1 meter of compressed dry leaves and thatch branches, trapping body heat down to sub-zero temperatures without fire.
